outputs.exact_statement:
For every sufficiently large prime $p$, there is a connective $p$-complete spectrum $X$ of exact fp-type two such that, for a standard form of $\mathrm{BP}\langle2\rangle_p^\wedge$, $$X\notin\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(\mathrm{BP}\langle2\rangle_p^\wedge).$$ The same spectrum satisfies $$L_2^fX\simeq L_2X,
 \qquad L_{T(2)}X\simeq L_{K(2)}X.$$

The map $f$ is flat and affine. The maps $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}A_2\to\mathcal M$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}A_{\mathrm{Haz}}\to\mathcal M$ are flat affine covers. In graded coordinates, the cooperation Hopf algebroid of the latter chart has arrow ring $$A_{\mathrm{Haz}}\otimes_{P,\eta_L}\Gamma_P
                  \otimes_{P,\eta_R}A_{\mathrm{Haz}}.$$

Let $A$ be a $k$-algebra with a locally finite continuous action of $Z$, and let $Z_m$ be the subgroup of index $p^m$. Suppose that $$A=\bigcup_{m\geq0}A^{Z_m}$$ and that the action on $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}A$ is geometrically free. Then $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}A\to\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A^Z)$ is an fpqc $Z$-torsor.

There is a flat affine groupoid stack $\mathcal N$ and a map $r:\mathcal M_k\to\mathcal N$ that quotients the vertical central $Z$-action on arrows. Its pullback is exact and identifies sheaves on $\mathcal N$ with sheaves on $\mathcal M_k$ having trivial vertical $Z$-action. Moreover $$f'=rf_k:\mathcal X_k\longrightarrow\mathcal N$$ is flat and affine. The weight line descends to $\mathcal N$, and $t=v_1$ is an invariant Cartier section of $\mathcal O(1)$ there.

There are equivalences $$\mathcal M_0[1/t]\simeq BZ,\qquad
 \mathcal N[1/t]\simeq\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}k.$$ The first is split by the law with $v_1=1$ and $v_{i>1}=0$.

The sheaves $T'$ and $T_k$ are $t$-monic. Set $T'_d=T'/t^d$ and $T_{k,d}=T_k/t^d$; their ordinary quotients also represent their derived multiplication cofibers. On the chart of Proposition 6, $$T'_d=C_{\mathrm{lc}}(G/\Lambda,R_d) =C_{\mathrm{lc}}(H,R_d),$$ with action $$(gF)(s)=g\bigl(F(g^{-1}s)\bigr) \qquad(g\in G,\ s\in G/\Lambda).$$ The inner value is acted on through the coefficient action on $R_d$. The analogous description of $T_{k,d}$ uses $G_{\mathrm{up}}/\Lambda$.

The ring $\Delta$ has a complete separated decreasing filtration given by the ordered weights $$\operatorname{wt}(x)=4,\qquad
 \operatorname{wt}(U_1)=\operatorname{wt}(U_2)=1,\qquad
 \operatorname{wt}(U_3)=3.$$ Its associated graded is the commutative polynomial ring $$\label{geom:graded-operations}
 \mathop{\mathrm{gr}}\Delta=k[\sigma x,A,B,C].$$ The element $x$ is normal, $\Omega=\Delta/(x)$, and the induced filtration gives $\mathop{\mathrm{gr}}\Omega=k[A,B,C]$. Here $A,B,C$ are the initial symbols of $U_1,U_2,U_3$.

For each flat affine groupoid stack used here, twisted periodic complexes admit the injective model structure with quasi-isomorphisms as weak equivalences and monomorphisms as cofibrations. It is stable, its fibrant objects have injective sheaf terms, and maps into a fibrant object are computed up to compatible chain homotopy. If a sheaf $W$ satisfies $\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^{>a}(W,-)=0$ for some finite $a$, maps from its pure shifts can be computed by applying $\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(W,-)$ termwise to any quasi-isomorphic replacement whose terms are $\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(W,-)$-acyclic.

The right derived functors of sections in the sheaf categories above commute with filtered colimits and are computed by the flat affine coinduced resolution. The resolution is compatible with closed base change. If $\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^{>a}(\mathcal O,-)=0$, its finite truncation gives a sections-acyclic resolution that computes [geom:sections-homotopy] on periodic complexes. In particular $\pi_*$ then commutes with filtered colimits and telescopes.
Invariantsof smooth $k$-linear $H$-modules have cohomological dimension at most $3$. The same is true for $G$ and for sections on $\mathcal N/(t^d)$, for every $d\geq1$.

Projective dimensions in the Ext sense satisfy $$\label{geom:dimension-bounds}
 \operatorname{pd}_{\mathcal N}(\mathcal O)\leq4,\qquad
 \operatorname{pd}_{\mathcal M_k}(\mathcal O),
 \operatorname{pd}_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)\leq5,\qquad
 \operatorname{pd}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal O)\leq6.$$ For sheaves on $\mathcal M_k$, the right adjoint of $r^*$ has $$\label{geom:central-derived-invariants}
 r_*M=\ker(c-1:M\to M),\qquad
 R^1r_*M=\mathop{\mathrm{coker}}(c-1:M\to M),\qquad R^{>1}r_*M=0,$$ where the kernel and cokernel descend to $\mathcal N$.

The category $\mathbf D(\mathcal N[1/t])$ is the category of $D$-periodic complexes of $k$-vector spaces. Every object is the sum, over the $D$ residue classes, of its pure homology objects, and every graded periodic map on homology is realizable.*

*The category $\mathbf D(\mathcal M_0[1/t])$ is the category of $D$-periodic complexes of smooth $Z$-representations over $\mathbb F_p$. Every object also splits as the sum of its pure homology objects. Maps can have an $\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}^1$ component, but a pure object has no self-map to its $2$-shift when $D>3$.
For each $j\in\mathbb Z$ there are no self-maps to the $2$-shift of $\widehat T'[j]$, $\widehat T_k[j]$, or $\widehat T_0[j]$.

There is an exact fully faithful functor $$\mathcal R:\mathop{\mathrm{Perf}}(\mathscr E)\longrightarrow\mathbf D(\mathcal N)$$ from perfect right dg modules which sends $\mathscr E$ to $\widehat T'$ and identifies its image with $\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(\widehat T')$. For a finite-cell module $\mathsf P$, its image is the homotopy limit of an actual compatible tower $Y_d$ of complexes whose terms are finite sums of shifts of $T'_d$.

For a finite-cell realization $Y=\mathop{\mathrm{holim}}_eY_e$ there are natural equivalences $$Y/t^d\simeq Y_d\qquad(d\geq1).$$ Under these equivalences, the tower projection is the intrinsic reduction map. The profinite topology on $\pi_iY$ obtained from the finite-level sections calculation is consequently its inverse-limit topology from $\pi_i(Y/t^d)$.*

*If $Y'$ is a retract of $Y$, let $e_d$ be the idempotent of $Y_d$ in the derived category induced by the idempotent defining this retract. Then $Y'/t^d$ is the summand of $Y_d$ split by $e_d$, and $$\pi_iY'=\varprojlim_d\operatorname{im}(\pi_i e_d)$$ with its intrinsic profinite topology.

Every $P\in\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(T')$ has finite $\pi_iP$ for every integer $i$. Now let $P\in\mathbf D(\mathcal N)$ have finite $\pi_iP$ for every integer $i$. For each integer $i$, the group $\pi_i\widehat P$ is naturally profinite, with the intrinsic inverse-limit topology from the finite groups $\pi_i(\widehat P/t^d)$. The vector space $W_i(\widehat P)=\pi_iL\widehat P$ has a locally compact Hausdorff $k$-vector-space topology obtained as the increasing union of the compact open images of $\pi_{i+sD}\widehat P$, for $s\geq0$. The image of $\pi_iLP$ is discrete and cocompact in this space.* *If $Q\in\mathbf D(\mathcal N)$ also has finite $\pi_jQ$ for every integer $j$, then every map $f:\widehat P\to\widehat Q$ induces continuous maps $\pi_i\widehat P\to\pi_i\widehat Q$ and $W_i(\widehat P)\to W_i(\widehat Q)$ for every integer $i$, in the topologies just described. No global map $P\to Q$ inducing $f$ is required. If $\widehat P\simeq\mathcal R(\mathsf P)$ for a perfect right dg $\mathscr E$-module $\mathsf P$, then under this identification the natural identifications of Proposition 20 and Lemma 21 match the profinite topology on $\pi_i\widehat P$ with the one obtained from the realization’s finite-level sections and intrinsic reductions. Consequently they match the compact images and the increasing-union topology on $W_i(\widehat P)$.

If $g\in H(i)\setminus H(i+1)$, then $$\ell(g)\le r_i:=\sum_{j=1}^i p^{\lfloor j/2\rfloor}.
 \label{op:digit-displacement}$$ The action of $H$ on $R$ is faithful. With $r_0=0$, one has $$\kappa:=\sum_{l\ge1}\frac1{N_l}\le\frac p{p-1}.
 \label{op:kappa}$$ Moreover, for every $s\ge1$, $$\Gamma_s\subset H_{p^s}\subset H(2s-1),
 \qquad N_{p^s}\ge p^{3(s-1)}.
 \label{op:congruence-index}$$
Suppose [op:parameters] holds, $X=p^r\le qb

There is a measure $ u\in\Delta^\Lambda$ with reduction $\delta_\gamma-\delta_1$ such that $$\int_H u(g)u_g^n=0\quad(0\le n25, the weighted operator $a$ satisfies $$a mod x=\delta_\gamma-\delta_1=U_3, \qquad \sigma(a)=C. \label{op:initial-symbol}$$

For such a matrix, the numbers $$\mathsf R(l,j)-\mathsf R(l,j-1)-\mathsf R(l+1,j)
                       +\mathsf R(l+1,j-1)
 \label{op:rank-matching}$$ are $0$ or $1$ and define a partial matching of rows with columns. The rank $\mathsf R(l,j)$ counts the matched pairs in its block. When entries are fixed in order of increasing depth $b=j-l$, a new match at $(l,j)$ is possible exactly when both its row and column are still unmatched and the corner entry avoids one specified scalar. That scalar is determined by smaller-depth entries. Decisions at a fixed depth are independent of one another.

Under [op:parameters], there is $a\in\mathscr E_0$ satisfying [op:initial-symbol] whose triangular matrix on $\Phi$ has the following properties.* 1. *For every fixed $J\in\mathbb Z$, only finitely many matched pairs $(l,j)$ satisfy $l\le J0$ and $N_0$ such that for every integer $N\ge N_0$, at least $cN^\beta$ columns in $[-N,0]$ and at least $cN^\beta$ rows in $(0,N]$ are forever unmatched.* *Here the matching is that of Lemma 27; the constants may depend on $p$.

For every degree $i$, the normalized overlap has an identification $$W_i(Y)=\mathcal Q\oplus\mathcal K, \label{glue:overlap-splitting}$$ compatible with the $t$-period identifications. The map $\pi_iY\longrightarrow W_i(Y)$ has finite kernel and compact open image. Each such image is commensurable with $$C_0^{\rm lat}=\mathop{\mathrm{im}}_{\mathcal Q}(F_0\Phi) \oplus(\mathcal K\cap F_0\Phi). \label{glue:standard-compact}$$ The topology of $\pi_iY$ is the intrinsic compact topology from its finite reductions, and the induced topology on the overlap is the locally compact topology in [glue:overlap-splitting]. Every fixed compact stage of this overlap is contained in the image of one sufficiently late $t$-translated group $\pi_{i+sD}Y$.

The vectors $(q_j,k_l)\in\mathcal Q\oplus\mathcal K$, indexed by the paired lists, are linearly independent modulo $C_0^{\rm lat}$. For every sufficiently large integer $N$, at least $cN^\beta$ pairs, for a fixed $c>0$, simultaneously satisfy $j\le N$ and $|l|\le N$. For these pairs, their kernel coordinates are linearly independent modulo $x^{qN+1}R$.

The object $U$ of [glue:definition-U] satisfies $$\pi_iU\text{ is finite for every }i,\qquad \widehat U\simeq Y\in\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(\widehat T'),\qquad LU\simeq V.$$ Under these equivalences the structure map $LU\longrightarrow L\widehat U$ is the chosen lattice map.

For every map $g:U\to P$ with $P\in\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(T')$, the induced map $$W_i(\widehat g):\mathcal Q\oplus\mathcal K
                    \longrightarrow W_i(\widehat P)$$ is continuous and sends each paired vector $(q_j,k_l)$ into the discrete lattice $\mathop{\mathrm{im}}(\pi_iLP\to W_i(\widehat P))$.

Let $\mathcal C$ be an idempotent-complete triangulated category, let $T_0,U_0\in\mathcal C$, and let $$\Psi:\mathcal C\longrightarrow\mathop{\mathrm{Perf}}(\mathscr B_0)$$ be an exact functor with $\Psi(T_0)\simeq\mathscr B_0$. Assume that $H(\Psi(U_0))$ is torsion as a right $S_0$-module in every degree and is nonzero in at least one degree. Assume also that, for every $P\in\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}_{\mathcal C}(T_0)$ and every map $g:U_0\to P$ in $\mathcal C$, $$\label{rew:obs:two-tests}
 H(\Psi(g))=0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 H\bigl((\Psi(g))^*\bigr)=0.$$ Then $U_0\notin\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}_{\mathcal C}(T_0)$.

Let $S_0$ be a domain whose left and right ideals are principal, and let $D_0$ be a positive even integer. Every finitely generated right $S_0$-module is a direct sum of a torsion module and a finite free module and has a finite free resolution of length at most one. Every perfect right dg module over $S_0[t^{\pm1}]$, with $|t|=D_0$ and zero differential, splits in its derived category into the $D_0$-periodizations of its shifted homology modules. In particular it splits as a finite sum of free shifts and a perfect module with torsion homology.

Let $k$ be a finite field, and let $\mathcal A$ be a complete separated filtered $k$-algebra such that $F^n\mathcal A=\mathcal A$ for $n\leq0$ and $$\mathop{\mathrm{gr}}\mathcal A=k[z_1,\ldots,z_d,c]$$ as a graded algebra, with all the displayed generators of positive integer degree. There is a filtered algebra $\mathcal S$ and a map $\mathcal A\to\mathcal S$ with the following properties:*

1.  *$\mathop{\mathrm{gr}}\mathcal S$ is the homogeneous localization of $\mathop{\mathrm{gr}}\mathcal A$ obtained by inverting all homogeneous elements outside $(c)$;*

2.  *$\mathcal S$ is separated and complete for its exhaustive filtration, which is allowed to have nonzero terms of negative degree;*

3.  *$\mathcal S$ is flat as both a left and a right $\mathcal A$-module.*

*For a finitely generated good filtered right module $M$, the corresponding microlocalized module is $M\otimes_{\mathcal A}\mathcal S$ and its associated graded is the same homogeneous localization of $\mathop{\mathrm{gr}}M$. The analogous assertion holds for left modules.

The ring $S$ is a domain, every left or right ideal of $S$ is principal, and $S$ has a two-sided Ore division ring of fractions. The operator $a$ constructed in Proposition 28 has no one-sided inverse in $S$. In particular $S/aS\ne0$, and this right $S$-module is torsion.

Suppose $a_1,b_1\in\Delta$ satisfy $$\bigl(\sigma(\bar a_1)\bigr)=(C)
 \quad\text{in }\mathop{\mathrm{gr}}\Omega=k[A,B,C],
 \qquad \sigma(\bar b_1)\notin(C).$$ Fix an integer $L_0\geq0$. There is a constant $c_0$, depending on the fixed chart, $L_0$, $a_1$, and $b_1$, such that for every $n\geq1$ the image of $$\{f\in x^{-L_0}R:a_1(f)=b_1(f)=0\}
       \longrightarrow K_0/x^nR$$ has $k$-dimension at most $c_0(1+n)^{1/3}$.

Let $a\in\Delta$ be the operator of Proposition 28, so that $\bar a=U_3$ and $\sigma(\bar a)=C$.* 1. *Suppose a right ideal $J\subset\Delta$ contains $a\Delta$, is right $x$-saturated, meaning $bx\in J\Rightarrow b\in J$, and satisfies $JS=S$. Then $J$ contains an element $b$ such that $\sigma(\bar b)\notin(C)$.* 2. *Suppose $b_0\in\Delta[x^{-1}]$ does not belong to $Sa$ and annihilates a $k$-subspace $V\subset\ker(a:K_0\to K_0)$. There is $b_1\in\Delta$ annihilating $V$ with $\sigma(\bar b_1)\notin(C)$.

Every element $b\in\Delta$ has an adjoint $b^\dagger\in\Delta$ for the continuous pairing $$\langle u,f\rangle=\mathop{\mathrm{CT}}_x(uf),\qquad u,f\in K_0.$$ Here $\mathop{\mathrm{CT}}_x$ extracts the coefficient of $x^0$ in a Laurent series. Modulo $x$, taking the adjoint induces group inversion on $\Omega=k[[H]]$. In particular it preserves the conditions that an initial symbol generate $(C)$ or lie outside $(C)$.

For the object $U$ of Proposition 32, let $g:U\to P$ be a map in $\mathbf D(\mathcal N)$ with $P\in\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(T')$. Then $$\label{obs:ghost-implication} H(\widehat g_{\mathscr B})=0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad H\bigl((\widehat g_{\mathscr B})^*\bigr)=0.$$ Both zero assertions mean that the corresponding induced homology maps vanish.
For the object $U\in\mathbf D(\mathcal N)$ constructed in Proposition 32, $$U\notin\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}_{\mathbf D(\mathcal N)}(T').$$

For $p>8$ there is a triangulated equivalence $$\mathcal F:h\mathrm{Sp}_E\longrightarrow \mathbf D(\mathcal M)$$ whose sheaf homology is naturally identified, under descent and the periodic regrading below, with the $E_*E$-comodule homology functor $E_*(-)$. Its suspension structure gives natural isomorphisms $$\mathcal F(\Sigma^jZ)\cong(\mathcal F Z)[j]
 \qquad(j\in\mathbb Z).$$

Let $\mathscr C_E=\operatorname{Comod}_{E_*E}$ be the ordinary abelian category of all graded comodules. Then $$\operatorname{Ext}_{\mathscr C_E}^{s}(M,N)=0
 \qquad(M,N\in\mathscr C_E,\ s>6).$$ This includes every internal grading shift. Let $\mathrm{Syn}_E$ be the Grothendieck prestable infinity-category of spherical hypercomplete sheaves of spaces on the site $\mathrm{Sp}_E^{\mathrm{fp}}$ of finite spectra $P$ with $E_*P$ projective over $E_*$, with covers the single maps surjective on $E$-homology. Its objects are connective synthetic spectra, and each satisfies $$X\simeq\lim_{i\geq0}X_{\leq i}\qquad(X\in\mathrm{Syn}_E).$$ The ordinary unbounded derived infinity-category $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}(\mathscr C_E)$ is left complete as well. For the topological potential stages of the unit shift algebra on this same $\mathrm{Syn}_E$, and the algebraic potential stages of the periodicity algebra on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}(\mathscr C_E)_{\geq0}$, the natural functors are equivalences $$\mathcal M_\infty^{\mathrm{top}}\simeq
       \lim_\ell\mathcal M_\ell^{\mathrm{top}},\qquad
 \mathcal M_\infty^{\mathrm{alg}}\simeq
       \lim_\ell\mathcal M_\ell^{\mathrm{alg}}.$$ These are the two convergence inputs $(\spadesuit5)$ of v2 Propositions 4.4 and 4.8.

For the regular quotient $b$ just constructed, $$\mathrm{BP}_*b\cong\Gamma_P\otimes_{\eta_R,P}B_2.$$ Under Landweber base change to $E$ and descent to $\mathcal M$, this comodule is the pure sheaf $T_{\mathbb Z}$. The corresponding comodule for $b_p^\wedge$ is $T_{\mathbb Z_p}$. Both sheaves are $p$-monic, and their reductions modulo $p$ equal $T_0$.

At an odd prime, the quotient $b$ has the standard Steenrod module $$H^*(b;\mathbb F_p)\cong
 \mathcal A//E(Q_0,Q_1,Q_2),$$ where $Q_i$ are the Milnor primitives and $E(Q_0,Q_1,Q_2)$ is their exterior subalgebra. In particular its completion is a standard form of $\mathrm{BP}\langle2\rangle_p^\wedge$.

In a twisted periodic derived category of period $D$, suppose a complex has homology only in one residue modulo $D$, with sheaf $W$ in a chosen representative of that residue. It is isomorphic to the corresponding pure object in either of the following cases:*

1.  *$W$ has projective dimension at most $a$ in the Ext sense and $D>a+1$;*

2.  *$W$ has injective dimension at most $b$ and $D>b+1$.*

*The assertion applies to every shift of the complex.

For every integer $j$,$$\begin{split}
 \mathcal F(\Sigma^jL_ES^0)&\cong\mathcal O[j],\\
 \mathcal F(\Sigma^jL_Eb)&\cong T_{\mathbb Z}[j],\\
 \mathcal F(\Sigma^jL_Eb_p^\wedge)&\cong T_{\mathbb Z_p}[j].
 \end{split}$$

Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an equivalence of the underlying categories of triangulated categories, and let $\mathcal D_0$ be a thick subcategory of $\mathcal D$. Then $$\{X\in\mathcal C:
       F(\Sigma^jX)\in\mathcal D_0\text{ for every }j\in\mathbb Z\}$$ is a thick subcategory of $\mathcal C$.

Let $p>8$, with $D=2(p-1)>12$, and choose the comparison of Theorem 44. Suppose $U\in\mathbf D(\mathcal N)$ satisfies $$\pi_iU\text{ is finite for every }i\in\mathbb Z,\qquad \widehat U\in\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(\widehat T'),\qquad U\notin\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(T'). \label{transfer:conditions}$$ Choose an $E(2)$-local spectrum $Z_{\rm sp}$ whose image under $\mathcal F$ is $$\widetilde U=i_*e_*r^*U\in\mathbf D(\mathcal M).$$ Then $$X_{\rm sp}=\tau_{\geq0}Z_{\rm sp}$$ is a connective $p$-complete fp-spectrum of fp-type at most $2$, and $$L_{E(2)}X_{\rm sp}\simeq Z_{\rm sp},\qquad X_{\rm sp}\notin \mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}_{\mathrm{Sp}_p^\wedge}(b_p^\wedge).$$ Here $b$ is the standard regular quotient of Proposition 47.

There is an exact functor $$Li^*:\mathbf D(\mathcal M)\longrightarrow
                 \mathbf D(\mathcal M_0)$$ which on a termwise $p$-monic complex is ordinary reduction modulo $p$. For $F\in\mathbf D(\mathcal M_0)$ it has a natural comparison triangle $$F[1]\longrightarrow Li^*i_*F\longrightarrow F
      \xrightarrow{\delta_F}F[2].
 \label{transfer:reduction-triangle}$$

Let $\delta:\mathop{\mathrm{id}}\to[2]$ be a natural transformation on a triangulated category. For an object $A$, consider the property that there is an integer $N\geq1$ such that $$\delta_{A[j]}^N:A[j]\longrightarrow A[j+2N]
 \quad\text{is zero for every }j\in\mathbb Z,$$ where the power denotes the successive natural transformations on the intervening shifts. No compatibility between $\delta_{A[j]}$ and $\delta_A[j]$ is assumed. This property is thick.*

*Suppose in addition that the cones of the maps $\delta_{A[j]}$ are shifts of $B(A[j])$, where $B$ is an exact functor. If $A$ has the property, then $A\in\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(B(A))$.

Suppose $U\in\mathbf D(\mathcal N)$ and $\widehat U\in\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(\widehat T')$. Set $F=e_*r^*U\in\mathbf D(\mathcal M_0)$. Then $$\widehat F\in\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(\widehat T_0).$$ The comparison obstructions of [transfer:center-triangle] and [transfer:reduction-triangle] are uniformly nilpotent over all shifts of $U$ and $F$, respectively.
If $U$ satisfies [transfer:conditions], then $$Li^*(i_*e_*r^*U)\notin\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(T_0).$$
The spectrum $X_{\rm sp}$ has fp-type exactly two.

There are equivalences $$L_2^fX_{\rm sp}\simeq L_2X_{\rm sp}\simeq Z_{\rm sp},
 \qquad
 L_{T(2)}X_{\rm sp}\simeq L_{K(2)}X_{\rm sp}.$$

The spectrum $Y'=L_{K(2)}X_{\rm sp}$ is locally fp. In the $K(2)$-local category it belongs to $$\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(E_2)
   =\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}\bigl(L_{K(2)}\mathrm{BP}\langle2\rangle\bigr).$$ Its Morava $E$-cohomology $E_2^*Y'$ is finitely generated over the ring of operations $E_2^*E_2$, and it is reflexive in the $K(2)$-local category.
For height-two Morava $E$-theory, $$\tau_{\geq0}E_2\notin\mathop{\mathrm{Thick}}(b_p^\wedge).$$

purpose: Counterexamples to the Hahn-Wilson conjecture at height two

coverage.checked_domain: Triangular matrices of size 1 to 3 over F_2 and F_5 on eleven hand-chosen instances including empty, diagonal, off-diagonal and crossing-pair cases
coverage.oracle_basis: Candidate pairs must have distinct rows and columns and be consistent with block ranks computed from largest nonvanishing minors

coverage.checked_domain: Same eleven instances; every block (l, j) with 0 <= l <= j < n is checked
coverage.oracle_basis: For each block the number of candidate pairs inside it is compared with the independently computed minor-based rank
